note: Signals carried over from the earlier register (7 to 9 Nov).

signals.summary: US forces made 'limited' strikes on an Iranian air-defence system near Qeshm Island on 6 Nov; Trump called them minor and said talks continue. Fox News said CENTCOM is preparing for possible renewed major strikes but has no new order, and officials noted the 9 Nov new moon favours operations. A Qatari two-stage plan would lift the US port blockade, then reopen Hormuz. The UAE foreign minister urged de-escalation in a 5 Nov call with Iran's.
signals.check: Watch for official US, Iranian and UAE statements and any NCEMA or ADCMC guidance over the next few days; confirm crisis, continuity and spares plans for loss of generation, gas or desalination supply are ready if major combat resumes.
signals.notes: Proposed by the system, to confirm. Opened the AP story on Al Jazeera (7 Nov), the Guardian and AP story republished by Finwire (7 Nov), ETV Bharat (AP, 7 Nov) and Capital Information (7 Nov, citing AP and Reuters). The last two describe the Qatari plan: the US lifts the port blockade and releases some frozen funds, Iran admits inspectors, then Hormuz reopens under a temporary arrangement; Capital Information says both governments have not yet accepted it. Fox News live page (6 Nov) for the CENTCOM and new-moon points; it does not say a date was chosen. Times of Israel (6 Nov, with Reuters) adds a Bloomberg report that a deal may be near. The National (6 Nov, citing WAM) for the UAE call. None of the pages reports an attack on a UAE site. Fits ER-02 if escalation is confirmed; follows SQ-0059 and SQ-0055.

signals.source: News wires: Reuters, AFP, DPA (via republishing sites)
signals.summary: UKMTO said the master of an outbound tanker reported an explosion at the port-side waterline about 16 nm east of Khasab, Oman, in the Strait of Hormuz; all crew were safe and the tanker continued under its own power. No cause was given. UKMTO reported it on 6 Nov; Fox News dates the incident to 5 Nov. On 6 Nov the IRGC claimed two more tankers caught fire and were immobilised in or near the strait; not independently confirmed.
signals.check: Confirm the Khasab incident and any JMIC threat update on the UKMTO and JMIC pages, and ask logistics whether inbound transformer, cable or meter shipments are delayed or rerouted.
signals.notes: Proposed by the system, to confirm. Opened the Reuters story on Devdiscourse (6 Nov 17:45 IST), the Fox News live page (6 Nov), which quotes the UKMTO notice and dates the incident to Thursday 5 Nov, and Iran International (6 Nov), which says UKMTO acted on a delayed report. Times of Israel (6 Nov) also reports it. UKMTO page not opened; vessel name and flag unknown. Update on SQ-0060: The National (6 Nov) names the tanker hit north of Qatar as Velos Sapphire, and Kurdistan24 (6 Nov) and the CBS News live page (6 Nov) say its operator reported one crew member killed. IRGC claim from CBS News and Kurdistan24, unverified. Fits ER-01 if confirmed; follows SQ-0060.

signals.source: The National: Abu Dhabi energy coverage
signals.summary: From 1 January 2027, Cabinet Decision No. 174 of 2026, the executive regulation of the federal traffic law, bars driving for more than nine hours in any 24-hour period and driving while fatigue affects safety. The Federal Traffic Council can amend the limit. Khaleej Times calls it a general obligation on drivers, not only professionals; The National has asked officials to confirm the scope.
signals.check: Get the official text (WAM or the UAE Legislation portal) to confirm scope and enforcement, then ask HSE and HR to check driving hours for field crews, standby and emergency call-outs and contractors before 1 January 2027.
signals.notes: Proposed by the system, to confirm. Opened The National (4 Nov, updated 5 Nov) and its follow-up analysis (5 Nov, updated 6 Nov, https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/uae/2026/11/05/drivers-hours-rule-will-improve-safety-but-cause-upheaval-analysts-say/), where an Arthur D Little analyst says the rule covers private and professional drivers alike and a road-safety expert says tachographs will be central to enforcement. Khaleej Times (4 Nov, updated 6 Nov) cites Article 7(2) and Federal Decree-Law No. 14 of 2024. Emirates 24|7 credits WAM; the WAM page (https://www.wam.ae/en/article/c3347tx-new-traffic-regulations-uae-take-effect-january) did not load, so the official text is unverified. Three days old but not in the register. No page mentions utilities or field service crews; how the limit applies to company fleets and call-out driving is unverified. No register risk covers workforce or HSE rules.

signals.source: News wires: Reuters, AFP, DPA (via republishing sites)
signals.summary: Reuters (6 Nov): LME three-month copper fell 0.5% to $13,775/t, a fourth daily fall, after touching $13,636, the lowest since 30 Jul, and was heading for a 2.6% weekly loss, the steepest since March, amid an AI-linked tech sell-off. Physical supply stays tight: Shanghai exchange stocks fell over 24% this week to 33,848 t, the lowest in almost three years, and the Yangshan premium hit a record $217.50/t. Aluminium fell 0.5% to $3,049/t.
signals.check: Ask Procurement whether cable, transformer and meter contracts are indexed to LME copper or aluminium and whether the dip is a buying window given tight physical supply; confirm prices on the LME site.
signals.notes: Proposed by the system, to confirm. Opened the Reuters story on MINING.COM (6 Nov 10:27). The LME page did not load, so prices were not checked against the exchange; single grade B source. Prices are volatile. ER-07 (critical minerals) is Closed, so not linked; follows SQ-0038 and SQ-0017.

signals.source: News wires: Reuters, AFP, DPA (via republishing sites)
signals.summary: US Central Command said a US aircraft disabled a St Kitts-flagged cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman on 7 Nov, firing precision munitions at its stern after it tried to breach the Iran blockade; Gulf News names it M/V Huda. UKMTO reported a bulk carrier in an incident with military forces about 18 nm east of Khor Fakkan, dated 7 Nov. On 8 Nov the UAE National Guard said it rescued 22 crew from a cargo ship fire in the Sea of Oman.
signals.check: Confirm the Khor Fakkan incident on the UKMTO site and whether it involves the ship US forces disabled or the one the UAE rescued; ask logistics whether transformer, cable or meter shipments through Khor Fakkan or Fujairah are delayed, rerouted or facing new war-risk charges.
signals.notes: Proposed by the system, to confirm. Opened the Reuters story on gCaptain (7 Nov, 14:04 PST), the AP story on WSLS (7 Nov), the Gulf News live blog (updated 8 Nov 08:21), which names M/V Huda, Arab News (8 Nov 02:02, with agencies) for the UKMTO Khor Fakkan advisory, and for the rescue the WAM story on Emirates 24|7 (8 Nov 08:37; only the opening lines loaded), Kuwait Times (KUNA, 8 Nov) and Gulf News (8 Nov). UKMTO and CENTCOM pages not opened. No page says whether the three reports involve the same ship; Arab News gives an inconsistent report time. Reuters adds that Tehran has threatened broad retaliation against Gulf infrastructure. Fits ER-01 if confirmed; follows SQ-0065.

signals.summary: CISA advisory ICSA-26-307-01 (3 Nov): Subnet Solutions PowerSYSTEM Center 2020 (to 5.29.x), 2024 (6.0-6.2) and 2026 (7.0-7.1) have two flaws rated CVSS 9.0: incorrect authorisation lets a low-privileged user reach admin-only resources (CVE-2026-63017), and SQL injection in the report designer (CVE-2026-63774). Sector: energy, worldwide. Fixes: 2020 Update 30, 2026 Update 1.1. Not remotely exploitable; no known public exploitation.
signals.check: Ask OT security whether PowerSYSTEM Center is used to manage substation devices or passwords; if so, confirm the version and plan the vendor update or the interim mitigations in the advisory.
signals.notes: Proposed by the system, to confirm. Opened the CISA bulletin of 3 Nov (https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USDHSCISA/bulletins/4317fd8) and the advisory's CISA CSAF file on GitHub (the url). The CISA web page (https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-advisories/icsa-26-307-01) did not load. Five days old but not in the register. Whether the product is installed is unknown. A vulnerability, not a campaign, so not linked to ER-03; relevant to it if the product is in use.

signals.source: Gulf News / Khaleej Times / TradeArabia: UAE business and utilities
signals.summary: EWEC says clean and renewable generation (nuclear, solar and wind) grew more than 1,000% from 2020 to 2025, from about 4,100 GWh to over 49,300 GWh, and now makes up almost 46% of Abu Dhabi's power generation, up from under 5% in 2020. It cites the four Barakah units (online 2020 to 2024), Al Dhafra Solar PV and Noor Abu Dhabi, and says reliability and security of supply were maintained.
signals.check: Confirm the figures in EWEC's report or the WAM story, and ask Network planning whether the rising nuclear and solar share is reflected in network operating and connection assumptions.
signals.notes: Proposed by the system, to confirm. Opened TradeArabia (5 Nov) and Gulf News (updated 6 Nov 10:09), which quotes EWEC Chief Assets Officer Mohamed Almarzooqi. The WAM story (https://www.wam.ae/en/article/c33pnfy-abu-dhabi-clean-energy-generation-1000-since-2020) did not load, so the figures are not checked against a grade A source. Three days old but not in the register. Progress report, not a risk event; context for ER-08.

signals.source: News wires: Reuters, AFP, DPA (via republishing sites)
signals.summary: A drone hit Iraq's Khor Mor gas field in the Kurdistan region late on 8 Nov, striking a gas storage tank and starting a fire; production and gas supply to the region's power plants stopped. The regional electricity ministry said about 2.8 GW of generation was lost. No casualties were reported and no group claimed it. The UAE's Dana Gas is a joint operator; Kurdish ministries called it a terrorist attack.
signals.check: Ask Network operations and the gas supplier whether contingency plans cover a sudden loss of gas to Abu Dhabi power and desalination plants, including load-shedding priorities and backup supply for water and sewage pumping stations.
signals.notes: Proposed by the system, to confirm. Opened the Reuters story on Internazionale (8 Nov, 22:48 CET), which says a single drone hit the LPG storage tank; the AFP story on Arab News (8 Nov 20:35 UTC, updated 9 Nov 00:36), which gives 11 pm (2000 GMT) and says gas supply to the region's power plants stopped; Al Jazeera (9 Nov), which quotes the electricity ministry at 2,500 to 2,800 MW and says hospitals and water treatment plants are being supplied from hydro and alternative-fuel plants; 964media (9 Nov) and investingLive (8 Nov). The 2.8 GW figure is from Reuters only among grade B sources, and AFP does not mention casualties. Restart timing unknown. No effect on the organisation's supply is reported. Strong fit to ER-02 (attacks on Gulf energy sites, generation outages) if a person confirms.

signals.source: The National: Abu Dhabi energy coverage
signals.summary: Siemens Energy's Middle East and Africa president told The National at ADIPEC it is adding shelters and barriers at existing Gulf power plants and considering partly underground designs for new ones to resist drone and missile attacks. Customers want larger stocks of long-lead critical components; with Hormuz shipping disrupted, it is looking at shipping large equipment in sections for site assembly. Gas turbines are 'completely sold out'.
signals.check: Ask Procurement whether lead times and Hormuz routing for transformers, switchgear and other long-lead network equipment have changed and whether strategic spares should rise; ask Asset management whether physical protection of key substations has been reviewed.
signals.notes: Proposed by the system, to confirm. Opened The National (dated 6 Nov, updated 8 Nov 06:23), an interview at ADIPEC. Single grade B source; no Siemens Energy release opened. The article also says grid infrastructure is exposed ('everybody knows where they are') and mentions a new USD 150 million Siemens Energy transformer factory in Dammam. It gives no figures for redesign costs or lead times. Three days old but not in the register. Context for ER-01 (equipment shipping and lead times) and ER-02.

signals.summary: UKMTO warning 199-26: a tanker caught fire about 8 nm NW of Khasab, Oman, at about 1920 UTC on 7 Nov and its crew was evacuated; no cause given. UKMTO also had a delayed report of an outbound tanker hit by an unknown projectile in Hormuz on 7 Nov, crew safe, no pollution. OSINT analysts tentatively name the burning ship as an ADNOC-chartered product tanker. On 8 Nov the IRGC claimed three tankers caught fire; not independently confirmed.
signals.check: Confirm on the UKMTO and JMIC pages, and ask Procurement and logistics whether inbound transformer, cable or meter shipments or fuel deliveries transit Hormuz this month.
signals.notes: Proposed by the system, to confirm. Opened The Maritime Executive (8 Nov 15:37), Arab Times (8 Nov, Muscat dateline) and JNS (8 Nov) for warning 199-26 and the 1920 UTC time, Iran International (8 Nov) and TASS (8 Nov) for the delayed projectile report, and the Gulf News live blog (updated 9 Nov 05:35) and Khaleej Times live blog (8 Nov) for the IRGC claim. UKMTO page did not load. The vessel name is OSINT only; The Maritime Executive does not say whether the two UKMTO reports involve the same ship, and says transits are roughly one to low double digits a day. The Maritime Executive is not in the sources list, so it was added for review (grade C). Follows SQ-0068. Fits ER-01 if confirmed.

signals.source: News wires: Reuters, AFP, DPA (via republishing sites)
signals.summary: Trump told CNN on 8 Nov that renewed US attacks on Iran were 'highly unlikely' to be needed if talks progress, depending on whether Iran signs 'a very strong agreement'; he said the US has identified infrastructure targets, including 38 bridges. On 7 Nov an IRGC spokesman said Iran's self-imposed 2,000 km ballistic missile range limit 'has been lifted'. Iran says it would answer renewed attacks by striking US and Israeli targets.
signals.check: Watch for official US, Iranian and UAE statements over the next days and any NCEMA or ADCMC guidance; confirm crisis and continuity plans for loss of generation, gas or desalination supply remain ready.
signals.notes: Proposed by the system, to confirm. Opened the Reuters story on Arab News (8 Nov 19:11 UTC, updated 23:42) and, for the IRGC remarks, the AP story on WSB Radio (7 Nov 11:38 UTC); Fox News via The Bullet (8 Nov) adds the spokesman's warning of 'surprises'. AP notes Iran is not known to have missiles beyond the old limit. Mixed signals: Reuters sees no sign of a large-scale US operation; the Gulf News live blog (updated 9 Nov 06:52) says Trump meets Qatar's prime minister on 9 Nov and said 'we're doing well' on ending the war, while the Khaleej Times live blog (8 Nov) reports Iran's foreign minister saying there have been no negotiations since the US midterms. No attack on a UAE site reported. Context for ER-02; follows SQ-0064.

signals.source: News wires: Reuters, AFP, DPA (via republishing sites)
signals.summary: Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said an Aramco administrative building in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District was the target of an 'attempted attack' on 8 Nov; falling shrapnel caused minor damage and no injuries were reported. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles fired at Riyadh. The Houthis claimed it as one of several attacks on Aramco sites.
signals.check: Ask HSE and Security whether shelter-in-place and evacuation procedures for head office and control buildings cover missile or debris alerts, and note any Houthi or Iranian statements naming UAE energy companies.
signals.notes: Proposed by the system, to confirm. Opened the AFP story on Dawn (8 Nov), which quotes the Saudi energy ministry and the coalition spokesman, and the UPI story on Yahoo News (8 Nov 15:23 UTC) for the Houthi claim and CNN-verified video of damage to several floors. The Khaleej Times live blog (8 Nov) also cites AFP and Reuters. CNN, NBC and France 24 pages did not load. No effect on Aramco operations or supplies is reported. Context for ER-02; follows SQ-0035.

signals.source: The National: Abu Dhabi energy coverage
signals.summary: The IEA's Renewables 2026 report projects the UAE will become the world's largest solar power generator per capita by 2031, above 4,000 kWh a person, against a global average of about 800 kWh. Middle East renewable capacity is expected to triple by 2031. The UAE's clean energy target (renewables and nuclear) was raised to 35% by 2030 to 2031.
signals.check: Confirm the figures in the IEA Renewables 2026 report, and ask Network planning whether solar and storage growth to 2031 is reflected in distribution capacity, voltage and protection planning.
signals.notes: Proposed by the system, to confirm. Opened The National (7 Nov, updated 08:33 UTC) and GreenTechLead (6 Nov), which says the IEA raised its UAE forecast, the UAE is developing battery storage and round-the-clock renewable projects, and the IEA's faster-growth case for the region needs improved transmission infrastructure. The IEA report page did not load, so the figures are not checked against the grade A source. The ranking is per capita, not total. Two to three days old but not in the register. Long-term context for network planning; related to SQ-0070.

new_sources.name: The Maritime Executive
new_sources.why: Added by the daily scan for review: maritime trade news covering Hormuz incidents, UKMTO reports and vessel identifications. Lead only: confirm with UKMTO, JMIC or official statements.
